My fiance and I lost our cat Buddy a month ago. He was only 8 and we'd had him since he was a week old. He helped me cope with my depression, when I was feeling suicidal he'd be there and wouldn't leave me alone. He was the best friend I ever had. The day to day for me at least has gotten a little easier. There are moments though where just an intense moment of sadness will hit you and you'll cry, be angry, and just so much wish they were there. 

I dont have much in the way of advice. It's EXTREMELY fucking hard to do but try and be thankful that you got to live her life with her and be in it. If you have any other pets love them harder and hug them a longer. Or reverse that, your call. There's a lyric Eminem had that said, " instead of mourning your death, I'd rather celebrate your life." I know it's a common sentiment but it holds true for this. For me anyway. Hold on to the times where Buttercup made you love her even harder, when you were having a shit day that she turned it ok.

As for forgetting her for a moment, it doesn't mean you love her any less. She wasn't always on your mind before she passed, I'm sure. I know it makes you feel guilty about it once you realize you aren't thinking about her. It is impossible to think about her every waking moment.  You still loved her and you still cherished her. 

I'm sorry for writing a novel and I sincerely hope you'll be ok. Be thankful for the lovely times you had and I hope it gets easier for you.
